findings: src/optimizer/rule/join_dependent_filter.cpp: the change extends the existing JoinDependentFilterRule so it also fires when the root is an AND with OR-of-AND children. That is the common shape after DistributivityRule factors out shared terms, or when a user writes an OR next to other conjuncts. Nothing in it refers to particular tables, columns, literals or queries.

Correctness: each derived term is an OR of single-table conjuncts taken from every branch, so it is implied by the original OR under three-valued logic. If the OR is TRUE, some branch is TRUE, and so is that branch's part for each table. The original OR is always kept. Volatile expressions are still excluded by ExtractConjunctedExpressions. ANY_JOIN conditions keep the same truth value, because the extra conjuncts are TRUE whenever the original is TRUE. This matches the semantics of the existing root-OR path.

Termination: derived conjuncts are flattened and appended only when no existing child of the root AND, and no conjunct already added in the same pass, is Equals() to them. On the next fixpoint iteration they derive the same conjuncts again and are filtered out. The derived per-table ORs reference only one table each, so DeriveFilter cannot fire on them again. The root-OR path now flattens instead of nesting, which keeps that dedupe working on the next pass.

Minor and not blocking: the dedupe relies on derived terms staying structurally equal to what is re-derived from the original OR. Any other rewrite rule that changed only the derived copies would break that. I could not find such a rule, because the derived terms are copies of subterms the same rules already see in the original.
Scope is one file and the change does what the issue says. No settings, tests or measurement code are touched.
